targets.title: Deliberative Abilities and Influence in a Transnational Deliberative Poll (EuroPolis).
targets.evidence_quote: The paper (Gerber et al., 2018a) and supplementary material (Gerber et al., 2018b) were, first, thoroughly studied in light of the claim that had to be reproduced. The claim that needs to be reproduced relates to the data in Table 2, column “Absolute opinion change (immigration)” in the paper (Gerber et al., 2018a, p. 1112); the full model is also shown in the online appendix, Table A11 (Gerber et al., 2018b).
targets.outcome_computational_quote: Reproduction outcome: Based on these criteria, the claim did reproduce.
targets.outcome_robustness_quote: Since Replicate Models in Table 1 and 2.do do-file also runs analyses on other datasets related to other data presented in the paper, which goes beyond the scope of this reproduction (for example, Table 1 in the paper), a do-file version that runs only the analyses needed for this single-trace claim was created simply by making the commands related to Table 1 in the do-file inactive (by putting * at the beginning of the command lines related to Table 1 data). This do-file, Replicate only Models in Table 2, runs on the SANDERS_Replication.dta file and performs multilevel linear model (Restricted Maximum Likelihood, REML) predicting opinion change on immigration position by a set of predictors and controls, needed to answer the single-trace claim. No other changes in the do-file were introduced.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The original N=174, coefficient .130 and SE .066 are reproduced within rounding, with p=.049 supporting the originally reported p<.05. Only the original model was re-run; unrelated commands were disabled and no alternative specifications were examined.
